verses.text: These are David's last words. This is what David son of Jesse declared, the man God raised up high, the one the God of Jacob anointed, the singer of Israel's beloved psalms:
“The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me. His word was on my tongue.
The God of Israel spoke. The Rock of Israel told me, ‘When someone rules people with justice and governs with reverence for God,
he's like the morning light at sunrise under a cloudless sky, like the sunshine that brings tender grass up from the ground after rain.’

Isn't this how God looks on my family? He's made an everlasting covenant with me, carefully arranged and secure in every detail. It holds all my salvation and everything I hope for. Won't he make it flourish?
But all the wicked are like thorns to be thrown away. You can't pick them up with your bare hands.
Anyone who handles them needs an iron tool or a spear shaft. They'll be burned completely right where they lie.”
These are the names of David's mighty warriors. Josheb Basshebeth the Tahchemonite was chief of the captains. He was also called Adino the Eznite. He killed eight hundred men at one time.

Next was Eleazar son of Dodai, who was descended from an Ahohite. He was one of the three mighty warriors with David when they challenged the Philistines gathered for battle and the men of Israel had pulled back.
Eleazar stood his ground and struck down Philistines until his hand cramped around his sword. The LORD gave a great victory that day. The people came back after Eleazar only to gather plunder.
Next was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines gathered together near a field full of lentils, and the people fled from them.
But Shammah stood in the middle of the field, defended it, and struck down the Philistines. The LORD brought about a great victory.
During harvest, three of the thirty leading warriors went down to David at the cave of Adullam. A company of Philistines was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.
David was in the stronghold at the time, and there was a Philistine garrison in Bethlehem.
David said wistfully, “If only someone would bring me a drink from the well by the Bethlehem gate!”
The three warriors broke through the Philistine lines, drew water from the well by the Bethlehem gate, and brought it back to David. He refused to drink it and poured it out to the LORD.

He said, “LORD, I could never drink this! It would be like drinking the blood of the men who risked their lives to get it.” So he refused to drink it. These were the things the three mighty warriors did.
Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, led the three. He fought with his spear against three hundred men and killed them, earning a name among the three.
He was the most honored of his group and became their commander, though he wasn't counted as one of the Three.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada came from a brave warrior of Kabzeel and did great deeds. He killed the two sons of Ariel from Moab. He also went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.
He killed a huge Egyptian who was carrying a spear. Benaiah went at him with a staff, snatched the spear out of his hand, and killed him with it.
These are the deeds of Benaiah son of Jehoiada. He earned a name among the three mighty warriors.
He was more honored than the Thirty but didn't reach the rank of the Three. David put him in charge of his guard.
Asahel, Joab's brother, was one of the Thirty. The others included Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem,
Shammah from Harod, Elika from Harod,
Helez the Paltite, Ira son of Ikkesh from Tekoa,
Abiezer from Anathoth, Mebunnai the Hushathite,
Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai from Netophah,
Heleb son of Baanah from Netophah, Ittai son of Ribai from Gibeah in Benjamin,
Benaiah from Pirathon, Hiddai from the streams of Gaash,
Abialbon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,
Eliahba from Shaalbon, the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,
Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam son of Sharar the Ararite,
Eliphelet son of Ahasbai, who was the son of the Maacathite, Eliam son of Ahithophel from Giloh,
Hezro from Carmel, Paarai the Arbite,
Igal son of Nathan from Zobah, Bani from Gad,
Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai from Beeroth, among those who carried the armor of Joab son of Zeruiah,
Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
and Uriah the Hittite. There were thirty-seven in all.
